text: The subject, Hina Yousaf, a 36‑year‑old student with a declared monthly income of PKR 25,000, received a rapid series of inbound IBFT transfers from at least sixteen distinct counterparties between 2 May and 11 May 2026, totalling approximately PKR 1,200,000. Each inbound payment ranged from PKR 15,000 to PKR 78,000 and was received into her HABB account (PK**HABB****7792) within hours of one another, a pattern flagged by the MULE‑01 typology (score 360 > alert threshold 300). Within the same 14‑day window, the account executed three large outbound wallet transfers to the same QuickPay e‑wallet (WLT****0932) on 4 May (PKR 184,000), 9 May (PKR 151,000) and 11 May (PKR 237,000), moving a total of PKR 572,000 out of the account. The outbound amounts represent a high proportion of the inbound funds and were transferred to a non‑bank wallet, a classic “layering” step in mule schemes. Additional red flags include two fraud recall requests from the sender banks (Fraud Desk note, 10 May) and the lack of any customer contact regarding the holds on the wallet transfers (L2 analyst note, 12 May). The subject’s profile (student, low declared income) is inconsistent with the volume and velocity of the transactions. These factors collectively indicate that the account is being used as a conduit for illicit funds, warranting the filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report.
